title: Composition of K-injective-normalized derived comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ for $i=0,1,2$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Assume every complex of each $\mathcal A_i$ admits a K-injective resolution, i.e. a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes. Let $F_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B_i$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with total right derived functors $(RF_i,\eta^i)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $Q_i:K(\mathcal A_i)\to D(\mathcal A_i)$ and $P_i:K(\mathcal B_i)\to D(\mathcal B_i)$ for localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$ put $c^i_a=(\eta^i_I)^{-1}\circ RF_i(Q_i a)$, the canonical resolution identification [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation].

For $0\leq i<j\leq2$ let $r_{ij}:\mathcal A_j\to\mathcal A_i$ and $s_{ij}:\mathcal B_j\to\mathcal B_i$ be exact additive functors, also denoting their termwise derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Suppose $r_{02}=r_{01}r_{12}$, $s_{02}=s_{01}s_{12}$ and $F_i r_{ij}=s_{ij}F_j$ on objects and morphisms. Use the induced canonical localization identifications throughout.

Suppose natural isomorphisms $\beta_{ij}:RF_i r_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{ij}RF_j$ are given and have the following normalization. For every K-injective $H$ in $\mathcal A_j$ and every K-injective resolution $a:r_{ij}H\to I$ in $\mathcal A_i$, the map $P_i(F_i a)$ is invertible and
$$(s_{ij}\eta^j_H)^{-1}\circ\beta_{ij,Q_jH}\circ(c^i_a)^{-1}=P_i(F_i a)^{-1}.$$
Then for every $L\in D(\mathcal A_2)$,
$$\beta_{02,L}=s_{01}(\beta_{12,L})\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}.$$
No $r_{ij}$ is assumed to preserve K-injective complexes.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined): K-injective evaluation; agent-written composition argument using the existing common-resolution lemma

proof.text: Fix a K-injective complex $H$ in $\mathcal A_2$. Choose K-injective resolutions $u:r_{12}H\to J$ in $\mathcal A_1$ and $v:r_{01}J\to I$ in $\mathcal A_0$, using the stated existence hypothesis. Set $w=v\circ r_{01}(u):r_{02}H\to I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $r_{01}(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence so is $w$; its target is K-injective. By [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], all the resolution comparisons below are isomorphisms. Write $A=s_{01}(c^1_u)$, $B=c^0_w$, $T=s_{02}(\eta^2_H)$, $X=P_0(F_0v)$, and $Y=P_0(F_0r_{01}(u))$. Here $T$ is invertible because [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] states that the derived unit is invertible on every K-injective complex, and functors preserve isomorphisms. We suppress only the canonical localization identifications stipulated in the item.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation and common-resolution statements; explicit composition calculation by NG.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-normalized-derived-comparison-common-resolution] with $(F,G,r,s)=(F_0,F_1,r_{01},s_{01})$, $N=r_{12}H$, and the resolutions $u:N\to J$, $v:r_{01}J\to I$. Its hypotheses hold: the two source categories have K-injective resolutions, $r_{01},s_{01}$ are exact, $F_0r_{01}=s_{01}F_1$, and $\beta_{01}$ has exactly its supplied normalization. Its successive-resolution formula gives
$$A\circ\beta_{01,Q_1(r_{12}H)}\circ B^{-1}=X^{-1}.$$
The invertibility of $X$ is part of the normalization at the K-injective $J$ and its resolution $v$. In particular the application makes no assumption that $r_{12}H$ or $r_{01}J$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation and common-resolution statements; explicit composition calculation by NG.

proof.text:
The normalization for $\beta_{12}$ at the K-injective $H$ and resolution $u$, after applying $s_{01}$, gives
$$T^{-1}\circ s_{01}(\beta_{12,Q_2H})\circ A^{-1}=Y^{-1}.$$
Indeed $s_{01}s_{12}=s_{02}$ identifies the unit factor with $T^{-1}$, and the stipulated localization identifications and $s_{01}F_1=F_0r_{01}$ identify $s_{01}(P_1(F_1u))$ with $Y$. Its invertibility follows from that same normalization and preservation of inverses by a functor. The normalization for $\beta_{02}$ at $H$ and resolution $w$ gives
$$T^{-1}\circ\beta_{02,Q_2H}\circ B^{-1}=P_0(F_0w)^{-1}.$$
These equations apply the given normalization at $H$ with precisely the resolutions $u$ and $w$.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation and common-resolution statements; explicit composition calculation by NG.

proof.text:
Let $C_H=s_{01}(\beta_{12,Q_2H})\circ\beta_{01,Q_1(r_{12}H)}$. Insert $A^{-1}A=1$ between these factors and use steps 2 and 3:
$$T^{-1}C_HB^{-1}=(T^{-1}s_{01}(\beta_{12,Q_2H})A^{-1})(A\beta_{01,Q_1(r_{12}H)}B^{-1})=Y^{-1}X^{-1}.$$
On the other hand $w=v\circ r_{01}(u)$ implies $P_0(F_0w)=X\circ Y$ by functoriality. Therefore step 3 reads $T^{-1}\beta_{02,Q_2H}B^{-1}=(XY)^{-1}=Y^{-1}X^{-1}$. Cancel the isomorphisms $T^{-1}$ on the left and $B^{-1}$ on the right. We have proved $\beta_{02,Q_2H}=C_H$ for every K-injective $H$.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation and common-resolution statements; explicit composition calculation by NG.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $L\in D(\mathcal A_2)$, choose a complex $N$ representing $L$ in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a K-injective resolution $N\to H$ by the hypothesis on $\mathcal A_2$. Localization inverts that quasi-isomorphism, giving an isomorphism $q:L\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_2H$ (composed with the chosen representation). Write $D_0=RF_0r_{02}$, $D_2=s_{02}RF_2$ and $C_L=s_{01}(\beta_{12,L})\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}$. Naturality of the two comparisons, expanded at $q$, yields
$$\begin{aligned}
D_2(q)C_L
&=s_{01}\bigl(s_{12}(RF_2(q))\circ\beta_{12,L}\bigr)\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}\\
&=s_{01}(\beta_{12,Q_2H})\circ s_{01}(RF_1(r_{12}q))\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}\\
&=C_H\circ D_0(q).
\end{aligned}$$
Here $r_{01}r_{12}=r_{02}$ and $s_{01}s_{12}=s_{02}$ give the endpoints. Naturality of $\beta_{02}$ similarly gives $D_2(q)\beta_{02,L}=\beta_{02,Q_2H}D_0(q)$.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation and common-resolution statements; explicit composition calculation by NG.

proof.text: Step 4 identifies $\beta_{02,Q_2H}=C_H$. Substituting this into the last two equations gives $D_2(q)\beta_{02,L}=D_2(q)C_L$. A functor sends the isomorphism $q$ to an isomorphism, so cancellation gives $\beta_{02,L}=s_{01}(\beta_{12,L})\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}$, as required. All K-injective complexes used were chosen in their own source categories; no functor $r_{ij}$ was assumed to preserve them.
